_comment: sim-robust-trajectory-clock-load-v1 bounded GPU proof recipe for the integration lane (twin-robot-in-store-boot-v1). Purpose: prove the trajectory host no longer raises 'trajectory clock/timeout failure' on a VALID trajectory under the heavy live_pose + arm-feed load. Root cause (coldlive sample 2, 2026-10-23, head 9406181): the execute loop's hard 'elapsed<0' check faulted on the sub-tick /clock-vs-/joint_states render-lead race -- start is anchored to a measured-feedback stamp (26.533) that led the node /clock (install 26.5167) by anchor_lag 0.017 s, so the next now()-start read -0.017<0 and 'TRAJ_HOST_FAULT trajectory clock/timeout failure' fired twice on a 2-point plan (npoints=2, goal_pos_tol=0.010); four earlier trajectories in the same run passed only because their first post-anchor now() happened to have caught up. Fix: trajectory_host.execute_clock clamps a within-FEEDBACK_RENDER_LEAD_S (0.2 s) negative elapsed to the start pose (same race feedback_fresh/reference_time already absorb), failing by name only on a genuine regression ('trajectory clock regression') or the frozen-sim WALL backstop ('trajectory clock/timeout failure').
_no_config_key: This fix has NO switch and NO runtime-config key: execute_clock always clamps, so an unaffected run is byte-identical and an affected run stops false-faulting. Nothing to merge into the mission runtime-config. Do NOT edit the ~/datasets mission-runtime JSON for this proof.
_how_to_run: Same bounded collect-only staging as sim-robust-collect-arrival-v1 under the FULL live_pose + arm-feed load: `scripts/run_mobile_restock.py ... --stop-after collect` with RESTOCK_TRANSFER_MODE=live_pose, RESTOCK_TRANSFER_CARRY=wrist_guard,weld, the masked_depth arm feed ON (host mast_depth OFF), visuals ON -- the exact cold live_pose config from coldlive sample 2. The code under test (twin.restock.trajectory_host) is the same process whether the run stops at collect or runs full; --stop-after collect bounds the GPU wall-clock and reaches the 2-point collect trajectory that faulted.

_suggested_env.RESTOCK_COLLECT_GROUND_TRUTH: UNSET (honest collect) OR 1 (GT collect) -- either exercises the same execute_clock path; the fault was in the trajectory host clock, independent of the sensing source
_suggested_env.RESTOCK_FEEDBACK_SIM_STALE_S: leave default (0.2) -- the clamp bound (FEEDBACK_RENDER_LEAD_S=0.2) is independent of this and already matches feedback_fresh

_expected_pass: The collect stage reaches and executes its arm trajectories (the 2-point TRAJ_HOST_PLAN among them) with NO 'TRAJ_HOST_FAULT trajectory clock/timeout failure' and NO 'TRAJ_HOST_FAULT trajectory clock regression' on a valid plan; collect either SUCCEEDS or fails fast for an unrelated NAMED reason. A healthy run logs 'TRAJ_HOST_START anchored ... anchor_lag=<small>s' followed by normal execution, never the immediate double clock-fault. Grep host-stack.log: `grep 'TRAJ_HOST_FAULT trajectory clock' host-stack.log` must be empty for the collect trajectories.
_gpu_rules: One GPU run at a time through flock on /tmp/aile-gpu.lock, never forced; never touch the whispr service (~2.2 GB VRAM). The validator may be holding the GPU -- do not take it.
